options.title: Shorten the go-pulse crossing
options.approach: In core, shorten the receive-to-transmit go pulse crossing (xpm_cdc_pulse u_p_go). Remove the output register after the edge detect, or use a lean pulse crossing with the same two synchroniser flops. Keep the order bus crossing, the synchroniser depth and the other crossings unchanged, and re-check the delay between pulse and bus that frame_src relies on.

gain.basis_note: cross_go adds 4 clocks. Removing the output register saves 1, and dropping the edge-detect stage as well saves at most 2. The two synchroniser flops stay, so the stage does not go below 2 clocks.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (4)

cost.note: Small RTL change. Rounds are needed for the CDC report and for the bus-settled (`stale`) check, which may need extra delay on the order bus.

risk.summary: An earlier pulse can reach frame_src before the order bus is settled. A lean pulse crossing keeps the two synchroniser flops, so the MTBF should be unaffected. Simulation cannot show the metastability effect, so a board run is needed.

options.title: Start the preamble without waiting for s_valid
options.approach: Let mac64_tx start the preamble word directly from the start pulse that frame_src receives, instead of one clock later on s_valid. This removes the fs_start register from the chain. The preamble does not depend on frame data and word 0 depends only on the configuration, so the data path is kept. The IP and UDP checksum logic and the PCS stay unchanged.

gain.basis_note: fs_start adds 1 clock, which is the most this change can remove. mac_preamble has 1.132 ns slack, so adding the start decode in front of it may use the slack and give 0.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (2)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The start path into the MAC is new and the MAC's pause and hold logic must be re-checked. The worst path (0.115 ns) is in frame_src ip_csum, so timing there must be watched.

options.title: Merge the receive gearbox extraction and descramble
options.approach: In pcs_rx, put the descramble and block-type decode (stage B) behind the same register as the block extraction (stage A), so that x_d, x_c and x_v are registered one clock earlier. The block-lock FSM keeps reading the block registers. No port of pcs_rx changes, and mac, decision and transmit logic are not touched.

gain.basis_note: rx_descramble adds 1 clock, so 1 is the upper bound. The stage file says the 192-bit shifter plus the 64-bit XOR tree did not close at 161 MHz, and slack on A and B is 1.544 ns and 2.215 ns. The merge may therefore not close, which gives 0.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (1)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: The merged path is likely to fail timing at first. Several rounds of restructuring the shifter and the XOR tree are expected.
cost.basis: iterations are the generator's estimate (a guess); wall time is those times the recorded Vivado run

gates: whole-core bench and the twin pass

timing met with WNS >= 0 after route
risk.summary: The 192-bit barrel shift followed by the descramble XOR tree in one clock may not meet timing. Timing is the main risk, not function.
risk.contract_note: The change is inside pcs_rx and its ports stay as they are.

options.title: Timing-assisted stage merges across the chain
options.approach: First try a different synthesis and placement strategy, for example performance-oriented directives, to gain slack on the receive and transmit paths. Then merge the register stages with the most slack: rx_descramble (2.215 ns) into the extraction and the fs_start stage into the MAC start. The decide register stays, because removing it puts the compare in front of the crossing flop. The go crossing and frozen blocks are not changed.

gain.basis_note: rx_descramble and fs_start add 1 clock each, so 2 is the upper bound. WNS is only 0.115 ns, so extra logic in these stages may need a tool-strategy gain first and the result could be 0.
gain.ceiling_basis: the clocks of the touched stages (2)

wall_minutes.basis: iterations x the recorded build time

cost.note: Each full Vivado run takes about 1177 s. Several strategy trials and then the merges are needed, and the whole-design re-verification adds rounds.
